changes.before: Input -2 is a valid integer. Why does this program still reject it?
changes.after: Accept input only when it is a readable number and an allowed count.

before: std::cin >> count attempts to extract an integer from standard input into count. Testing the stream in if reports whether extraction succeeded. For the worked example, type 3 and press Enter. A live terminal waits for input; end-of-input takes the failure branch.
A successfully extracted integer can still be unsuitable. count >= 0 rejects negative counts even though they are valid integers.
The && form checks extraction before the nonnegative rule. On extraction failure, use the error branch rather than assuming the stored number is valid.

Formatted extraction reads a numeric token, not a guarantee that the entire line contained only that number. Extra trailing characters can remain unread. This example ends after one attempt; a retry loop must also recover the stream state and discard unsuitable input.
Expected output or behavior: Accepted: 3. Local compiler test evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

Optional local transfer task: Try a valid positive count, zero, a negative count, a nonnumeric token, and end-of-input. Distinguish extraction failure from a rejected but valid integer. You may trace this without a compiler; finishing the reading is not proof of a local run.
after: std::cin reads input from the terminal. std::cin >> count tries to read an integer into count. An if condition can test whether that read succeeded. A terminal may wait until you type something or end the input.
A readable number may still break your program's rules. count >= 0 allows zero and positive counts. It rejects negative counts.
The && operator checks the read first. Only if that succeeds does it check count >= 0. The success branch runs only when both checks pass.
Reading an integer does not check the whole line. Text after the number can remain unread. Checking a complete line needs an extra step beyond this example.
The program prints Accepted: 3. It could read the integer, and three is not negative.
This program handles one attempt and then ends. A program that asks again after a failed read must first clear the input error and remove the unwanted input.

before.question: Input -2 is a valid integer. Why does this program still reject it?
choices: The separate nonnegative domain rule fails after extraction succeeds.
C++ cannot extract any signed integer.
The stream automatically changes -2 into zero.
before.explanation: The input passes integer extraction but fails the application’s count rule.

after.question: Why does this program reject the input -2 even though it is an integer?
choices: The number is readable, but it fails the rule that counts must be zero or more.
Reading the input automatically changes -2 into zero.
after.explanation: Reading -2 succeeds. The separate count >= 0 check is false, so the error branch runs.
